item.title: ‘Happy Gilmore 2’ Was the Most-Streamed Non-Kids Movie of the Year
item.description: Otherwise, "KPop Demon Hunters" would have won this award by a mile.

item.title: ‘Shrinking’ Season 3 Can’t Follow Its Own Advice
item.description: After finally pushing past its faulty premise, Apple's nice-core comedy enters Season 3 fully prepared to blossom into its best self. Instead, it wilts in a dreary year teeming with unfulfilled plans.

item.title: San Francisco’s Castro Theatre to Reopen with Premiere of A24’s ‘Pillion’
item.description: Closed since 2022 for renovations, the beloved San Francisco venue will host director Harry Lighton's film on Thursday, February 12.

item.title: Gregg Araki Thinks Sex Is Coming Back to Screens Thanks to Films and Shows Like ‘Heated Rivalry’ — and Hopefully, ‘I Want Your Sex’
item.description: Araki was joined by his "I Want Your Sex" stars Cooper Hoffman, Chase Sui Wonders, and Mason Gooding at the IndieWire Studio, presented by Dropbox.

item.title: ‘The Only Living Pickpocket in New York’ Review: An Old School Thief Holds on in the Age of Apple Pay
item.description: Sundance: Produced under Rian Johnson’s T Street banner, writer-director Noah Segan's New York picture breathes new life into the subgenre.

item.title: ‘In the Blink of an Eye’ Review: Andrew Stanton’s First Live-Action Movie Since ‘John Carter’ Is a Dreadful Straight-to-Hulu ‘Cloud Atlas’ Ripoff
item.description: Sundance: Telling three parallel stories at various points in time, Stanton's film spans 47,000 years in search of a single believable moment.

item.title: John Wilson on the Anxiety of Secretly Shooting the Kardashians in ‘History of Concrete,’ and Getting Recognized After His HBO Show
item.description: The director of Sundance smash documentary "The History of Concrete" joined the IndieWire Studio at Sundance to talk about his filming style, which often involves going rogue in spaces like GQ's Man of the Year dinner.

item.title: Mind-Bending Sundance Doc ‘Ghost in the Machine’ Asks the Hard Questions About AI’s Origins and Potential Misuses
item.description: Documentary filmmaker Valerie Veatch joined IndieWire's Sundance Studio to discuss her artificial intelligence essay film, "Ghost in the Machine."

item.title: The 2026 BAFTA Nominations Imply a Different Version of the Same Oscars Conclusions
item.description: The 2026 BAFTA Awards nominations provided more context for how Oscar nominations shook out, but have not exactly changed who the frontrunners are in the major categories.

item.title: ‘Take Me Home’ Review: A Sensitive Family Drama Upended by an Unearned Conclusion
item.description: Sundance: Liz Sargent's debut film is an admirably lived-in drama about a family in distress that retreats into fantasy rather than seeing through its complications.
